item.title: runit in Practice: Root and Non-Root Services
item.description:
runit is small enough to explain in a few sentences, but the details matter when you actually want a service to start at boot, restart after a crash, and log properly. This guide covers both sides of the same system:

  • System services live in /etc/sv, are enabled by symlinking them into /var/service, and are managed by root.
  • User services live in a directory owned by a normal user and are managed by that user without sudo.

The second part is the interesting one. It uses a small root-owned supervisor that drops privileges once, then lets the user create and control services forever after. That is exactly how the runsvdir-nvru + PipeWire setup works.
